social.title: Tailgate a Carolina Panthers Home Game
social.description: NFL Sunday in an uptown stadium you can walk to from anywhere in the centre, with the tailgate lots filling up four hours before kickoff.
social.bonus: Get to a tailgate before the gates open and eat something a stranger cooked.

social.title: Sing at Petra's in Plaza Midwood
social.description: A dark piano bar and cabaret on Commonwealth Avenue running drag, karaoke, open mics and dance parties, with a back patio and a proper NC beer list.
social.bonus: Put your name down for karaoke before you have had a second drink.

social.title: Watch the Hornets at Spectrum Center
social.description: NBA basketball right in the middle of uptown, with a teal crowd and forty-one chances a year to get a cheap upper-deck seat on a weeknight.
social.bonus: Get to your seat in time for warmups, not the tip-off.

social.title: Join the Supporters' Section for Charlotte FC
social.description: This club drew the biggest crowd in MLS history at its first home game, and Bank of America Stadium on a match night is the loudest thing in the Carolinas.
social.bonus: Stand and sing in the supporters' section for the entire ninety minutes.

social.title: Take the Patio at The Suffolk Punch
social.description: A brewery, restaurant and coffee bar in one, right on the Rail Trail in South End, with a big outdoor bar and a patio that fills up from four onwards.
social.bonus: Walk there along the Rail Trail rather than driving.

social.title: Drink at Heist Brewery, Reopened in NoDa
social.description: Two years dark after a kitchen fire, Heist came back over Memorial Day weekend 2026 with more seating, the old menu favourites and brunch.
social.bonus: Order one of the IPAs they brought back and ask a bartender about the fire.

social.title: Take a Knights Game at Truist Field
social.description: A Triple-A ballpark dropped into the skyline, where the outfield view is office towers and the beer selection is better than most bars.
social.bonus: Get a seat on the outfield terrace rather than behind the plate.

social.title: Get Into Dot Dot Dot
social.description: A storage unit behind the Park Road Shopping Center turned screen-free members' cocktail bar, where ten dollars a year gets you and three guests in.
social.bonus: Buy the membership at the door and bring someone who does not know where you are going.

social.title: Drink Nineteen Floors Up at Merchant & Trade
social.description: The rooftop of the Kimpton Tryon Park Hotel, level with the office towers, with four separate zones and the best skyline view in the city.
social.bonus: Get a seat on the open terrace rather than the indoor bar.

social.title: Drink at NoDa Brewing's North End Taproom
social.description: The brewery that put Charlotte beer on the map, in a big North End taproom with a beer garden, events most nights and Hop Drop 'n Roll on tap.
social.bonus: Try a beer that is only available in the taproom.

social.title: See a Band at the Neighborhood Theatre
social.description: A 1940s cinema on North Davidson turned independent music room in 1997, small enough that the band can see your face.
social.bonus: Get to the front and stay there for the whole headline set.

social.title: Catch a Show at The Fillmore Charlotte
social.description: A two-thousand-capacity room at the AvidXchange Music Factory with a standing floor, plus the smaller Underground next door for the acts on the way up.
social.bonus: Buy a ticket for the Underground show instead of the main room.

culture.title: Visit the Original Mint at Mint Museum Randolph
culture.description: The building was the first branch of the United States Mint, opened in 1837, moved stone by stone to Eastover and turned into North Carolina's first art museum.
culture.bonus: Find where the coins were actually struck.

culture.title: Take a Night at Belk Theater
culture.description: Blumenthal Arts' 2,100-seat main hall on Tryon Street, where the Charlotte Symphony, the opera and the big touring Broadway runs all land.
culture.bonus: Dress properly for it and get a drink in the lobby at the interval.

culture.title: Visit the Bechtler Museum of Modern Art
culture.description: One family's mid-20th-century European collection in a Mario Botta building with Niki de Saint Phalle's gold Firebird out front.
culture.bonus: Find the Giacometti and work out who in the family bought it.

culture.title: Catch Open Studios at the McColl Center
culture.description: A burnt-out Gothic church on North Tryon rebuilt as an artist residency, which periodically throws its studio doors open so you can talk to whoever is working inside.
culture.bonus: Ask one artist what they are actually trying to do.

culture.title: Spend an Hour in the Harvey B. Gantt Center
culture.description: African-American art, music and history in a building whose facade quotes the quilt patterns of the Brooklyn neighbourhood that once stood nearby.
culture.bonus: Find out what happened to Brooklyn, Charlotte, before you leave.

culture.title: Do the Banking at the NASCAR Hall of Fame
culture.description: A curved ramp of real race cars set at the actual banking angle of a superspeedway, plus racing simulators and a pit crew challenge.
culture.bonus: Beat someone in your group on the simulator.

culture.title: See the Collection at Mint Museum Uptown
culture.description: Five floors of craft, design and contemporary art in a glass building on Tryon Street, with a five-storey atrium window facing the city.
culture.bonus: Spend ten minutes with a single object in the craft and design collection.

culture.title: Stand Inside the Hezekiah Alexander Rock House
culture.description: The oldest surviving building in Mecklenburg County, a 1774 stone house on the grounds of the Charlotte Museum of History.
culture.bonus: Work out how the house was built before you read the panel that tells you.

8ball.title: Greenway Ghost Ride
8ball.description: Get on the Cross Charlotte Trail anywhere, ride until the greenway physically ends, and find your way home by whatever neighbourhood you land in.
8ball.bonus: Eat wherever you end up, even if it is a petrol station.

8ball.title: NoDa Dice Roll
8ball.description: Start at 36th and North Davidson, roll a die, and enter the nth door on your left. Whatever it is, you stay for one round. Repeat three times.
8ball.bonus: Only talk to people who were already inside when you arrived.

chill.title: Browse Park Road Books
chill.description: Charlotte's only full-service independent bookshop, in the Park Road Shopping Center since 1977 and open until nine on weeknights.
chill.bonus: Leave with a book from a section you never shop in.

chill.title: Dig the Bins at Lunchbox Records
chill.description: New and used vinyl on Central Avenue with a bias towards indie, punk, metal, funk and jazz, and a back room where bands actually play.
chill.bonus: Ask the person behind the counter what they have been playing all week and buy it.

chill.title: Take the Long Way Around Freedom Park
chill.description: Ninety-eight acres of lawn, lake and shade in Myers Park that function as Charlotte's back garden, with pedal boats on the water in summer.
chill.bonus: Take out a pedal boat and make a full circuit of the lake.

chill.title: Watch Planes Land from the Airport Overlook
chill.description: A free city-built viewing park beside the runway at Charlotte Douglas, with picnic tables, a speaker piping in the tower radio and a jet every ninety seconds.
chill.bonus: Identify three different aircraft types by sight before you leave.

chill.title: Take a Wine Flight at Foxcroft Food & Wine
chill.description: A wine bar that grew into a proper restaurant, with monthly tastings across its SouthPark, Dilworth and Waverly rooms and staff who will actually teach you something.
chill.bonus: Take a flight of things you cannot pronounce and name your favourite.

chill.title: Wander Daniel Stowe Botanical Garden
chill.description: Three hundred and eighty acres on Lake Wylie in Belmont, with a glass orchid conservatory and fountain gardens that are almost empty on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Find the orchid conservatory and stay in it for ten minutes.

chill.title: Have Coffee at 7th Street Public Market
chill.description: Not Just Coffee inside the uptown market, where they will talk you through a pour-over and the whole building is worth an hour afterwards.
chill.bonus: Order a pour-over instead of your usual and ask where the beans came from.

chill.title: Spend an Afternoon at Camp North End
chill.description: Seventy-six acres of former Ford assembly plant and missile factory now full of murals, makers, food and bars, with the industrial bones left visible.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest piece of original signage still on a building.

chill.title: Lie on the Lawn at Romare Bearden Park
chill.description: Five and a half acres of lawn, water features and terraces wedged between the skyline and the ballpark, best used before a Knights game.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to watch the office tower lights come on.

chill.title: See Something Strange at the Independent Picture House
chill.description: A nonprofit four-screen arthouse in a converted warehouse north of NoDa, run by the Charlotte Film Society, showing what nowhere else in the city will.
chill.bonus: Buy a ticket for the film with the least familiar title on the board.

foodie.title: Order the Fried Chicken at Haberdish
foodie.description: A Michelin-listed mill-town kitchen on North Davidson serving family-style Southern food and a serious cocktail list under a ceiling of textile-mill artefacts.
foodie.bonus: Order every side dish on the menu for the table.

foodie.title: Order Soul Food at Mert's Heart & Soul
foodie.description: Two decades on College Street doing Low Country and soul food, and the one uptown restaurant that locals and visitors both actually want to eat in.
foodie.bonus: Get the salmon cakes and the collards, and finish the cornbread.

foodie.title: Eat at Lang Van on Shamrock Drive
foodie.description: A strip-mall Vietnamese room in east Charlotte, open since 1992, that every chef in this city will tell you to go to before they mention their own restaurant.
foodie.bonus: Order something from the menu that nobody at the table can identify.

foodie.title: Have Dinner in the Church at Supperland
foodie.description: A restored midcentury church in Plaza Midwood turned into a Southern steakhouse, where you eat under stained glass with the organ pipes still in place.
foodie.bonus: Sit in the nave rather than the side room, and order something cooked over fire.

foodie.title: Eat in the Mill House at The Goodyear House
foodie.description: A restored 1900s mill worker's house in NoDa where Chris Coleman cooks a small, sharp Southern menu with a porch worth waiting for.
foodie.bonus: Get a table on the porch, even if it means waiting for one.

foodie.title: Take a Salted Caramel Brownie from Amelie's
foodie.description: A French bakery in NoDa done up like a Parisian flea market, with a pastry case worth the detour and the brownie that Charlotte argues about.
foodie.bonus: Order the brownie and a macaron and decide which one wins.

foodie.title: Graze Your Way Through Optimist Hall
foodie.description: A converted textile mill north of uptown holding twenty-plus stalls, from Dumpling Lady to Nashville hot chicken, plus bars at both ends.
foodie.bonus: Build a meal from three different stalls and eat it all at one table.

foodie.title: Get a Made-to-Order Doughnut at Milkbread
foodie.description: The Kindred family's all-day cafe in Davidson, open 7am to 9pm, doing premium doughnuts to order and a crispy chicken sandwich from a James Beard-nominated kitchen.
foodie.bonus: Order the doughnuts and eat them in the car before you leave the car park.

foodie.title: Order the Sandwich at Bossy Beulah's
foodie.description: A chicken shack built around one very good fried chicken sandwich, with a patio and a queue that moves fast.
foodie.bonus: Get the spicy version and finish it without a drink.

foodie.title: Get the Brisket at Noble Smoke
foodie.description: Jim Noble's hickory pit on Freedom Drive cooks whole hog the old Carolina way alongside Texas-style brisket, and five years in it has hit its stride.
foodie.bonus: Order both the Eastern and Lexington sauce and pick a side out loud.

foodie.title: Hit Oyster Happy Hour at Sea Level NC
foodie.description: North Carolina oysters shucked to order in the base of the Hearst Tower uptown, at a dollar fifty a piece from two until six.
foodie.bonus: Eat a dozen and taste the difference between two growing regions.

foodie.title: Eat a Cheeseburger at Brooks' Sandwich House
foodie.description: A cash-only walk-up window on North Brevard that has been making the same chilli cheeseburger since 1973 and closes at three in the afternoon.
foodie.bonus: Bring cash, get there before eleven and eat standing at the window.

adventure.title: Ride Fury 325 at Carowinds
adventure.description: A 325-foot giga coaster that crosses the North Carolina and South Carolina state line at 95 miles an hour, and is still one of the best in the world.
adventure.bonus: Ride Fury in the front row and again in the back row on the same day.

adventure.title: Ride the Anne Springs Close Greenway
adventure.description: Two thousand acres of trail, gravel and lake just over the state line in Fort Mill, with bike rental on site and a proper swimming lake in summer.
adventure.bonus: Swim in Lake Haigler after you finish riding.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike the Sherman Branch Trails
adventure.description: Charlotte's best flowy singletrack, east of the city off Rocky River Road, with a beginner loop and plenty of technical extras to get lost in.
adventure.bonus: Clean one feature you walked past on your first lap.

adventure.title: Ride the Rail Trail from South End to Uptown
adventure.description: A paved corridor beside the light rail linking breweries, murals and patios, which is by far the best way to see how fast this city is changing.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every mural you have not photographed before.

adventure.title: Summit Crowders Mountain
adventure.description: Thirty-five minutes west of the city, a genuine rock summit with a stair climb at the end and the Charlotte skyline visible from the top on a clear day.
adventure.bonus: Take the Rocktop Trail rather than the easy route, in both directions.

adventure.title: Raft the Channel at the U.S. National Whitewater Center
adventure.description: The world's largest man-made whitewater river runs in a loop twenty minutes from uptown, throwing genuine Class III and IV rapids at you all afternoon.
adventure.bonus: Get thrown out of the raft at least once and climb back in unassisted.

adventure.title: Chase Waterfalls at South Mountains State Park
adventure.description: Ninety minutes northwest, an eighty-foot waterfall at the end of a real climb, in the closest thing to proper mountains you can reach from Charlotte in a morning.
adventure.bonus: Get in the water at the base of High Shoals Falls.

adventure.title: Run the Greenway from Midtown to Freedom Park
adventure.description: The Little Sugar Creek Greenway threads out of Midtown under the tree canopy and delivers you to the best park in the city without crossing a road.
adventure.bonus: Finish with a lap of the Freedom Park lake before you stop your watch.

adventure.title: Kayak Lake Norman from Ramsey Creek Park
adventure.description: The largest man-made lake in the Carolinas, with a public launch and beach at Ramsey Creek and quiet coves to paddle into within minutes.
adventure.bonus: Paddle far enough out that you cannot see the boat ramp.

adventure.title: Walk the Lakeshore at McDowell Nature Preserve
adventure.description: Eleven hundred acres on Lake Wylie with seven miles of trail through old hardwood and a shoreline path that feels an hour from any city.
adventure.bonus: Hike the full Four Seasons Trail without turning back early.

adventure.title: Drive a Stock Car at Charlotte Motor Speedway
adventure.description: You get an 800-horsepower stock car, a helmet and the actual 1.5-mile banked oval that NASCAR races on in Concord.
adventure.bonus: Beat the speed of everyone else in your group.

adventure.title: Jump with Skydive Carolina in Chester
adventure.description: A family-run dropzone forty-five minutes south of Charlotte that has been putting first-timers out of aeroplanes since 1986.
adventure.bonus: Keep your eyes open for the entire freefall.

adventure.title: Climb at Inner Peaks in South End
adventure.description: Bouldering and rope climbing on South Tryon, open from six in the morning, with day passes and rental shoes for people who have never touched a wall.
adventure.bonus: Get to the top of one roped route without taking a rest on the rope.

adventure.title: Paddleboard Mountain Island Lake at Latta
adventure.description: A 1,300-acre nature preserve on a quiet lake where the shoreline is protected, so the water is flat and the view is nothing but trees.
adventure.bonus: Stand the whole way out and the whole way back.

adventure.title: Throw a Round at Renaissance Park Disc Golf
adventure.description: A championship-level course south of uptown with real elevation and water carries, free to play and busy with people who are much better than you.
adventure.bonus: Par the hardest hole on the course.

adventure.title: Try Deep Water Solo at the Whitewater Center
adventure.description: Climb an overhanging wall with no rope and no harness, because the only thing under you is the river. Plus a full ropes course and zip lines on the same pass.
adventure.bonus: Fall off from as high up the wall as you can make yourself go.
